topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the session by outlining the lecture's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Pathogen recognition and pattern recognition receptor signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects microbial and damage signals through pattern recognition receptors and downstream inflammatory complexes.

topics.label: Sentinel cell activation and leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated sentinel cells signal the vascular endothelium to guide leukocyte extravasation and migration to sites of infection.

topics.label: Lymphatic drainage and immune cell trafficking to lymph nodes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how dendritic cells use the lymphatic drainage system to carry antigens from infected tissues to lymph nodes for adaptive immune priming.

topics.label: Systemic inflammatory complications and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the pathological cardiovascular consequences and high mortality resulting from excessive systemic cytokine production.

topics.label: Mechanisms of inflammatory resolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the passive decay processes and active stop signals that terminate inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Tissue repair, chronic inflammation, and granuloma formation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the wound healing process and the development of chronic inflammatory structures when damage or infection persists.

topics.label: Closing remarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture and announces the topic for the next session.
